title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 139
paragraphs: This much I can say with certainty from my own knowledge. What follows is reported as a secret matter and not openly discussed: the body of a Persian man is not buried until it has been torn by a bird or a dog. I know for certain that the Magians do this, since they practice it openly. The Persians coat the body in wax before putting it in the ground. The Magians are very different from other men and from the Egyptian priests. The Egyptian priests scrupulously avoid killing any living creature except those they sacrifice. The Magians, however, kill everything with their own hands except dogs and humans. They kill ants, snakes, flying creatures, crawling creatures—everything—and regard it as a great achievement. Let this custom remain as it has always been, and I will return to my earlier narrative.
